panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 3 panels (A, B, C). A: Panel A is a clinical photograph of a pediatric patient with purple striae, explicitly attributed to prednisolone-induced iatrogenic Cushing's syndrome. [raw subtype: iatrogenic glucocorticoid-induced Cushing's syndrome] B: Panel B directly shows the captioned rounded, full facial appearance of moon facies in a child with prednisolone-associated Cushing's syndrome. [raw subtype: iatrogenic glucocorticoid-induced Cushing's syndrome] C: Panel C is a clinical photograph showing extensive purple abdominal and truncal striae explicitly associated with sustained glucocorticoid excess and iatrogenic Cushing's syndrome. [raw subtype: iatrogenic glucocorticoid-induced Cushing's syndrome]

panels.figure_caption: Patient three: purple striae, moon facies, and truncal skin changes in a paediatric patient with iatrogenic Cushing's syndrome secondary to prednisolone therapy (A) Purple striae over the forearm and hand in a 12-year-old boy maintained on oral prednisolone for epileptic encephalopathy, consistent with glucocorticoid-induced dermal atrophy and connective tissue catabolism. (B) Moon facies demonstrates a characteristic rounded facial contour and facial fullness consistent with cortisol-mediated fat redistribution. Face is de-identified to protect the identity of the minor patient. (C) Purple striae over the truncal and abdominal region, a well-recognised cutaneous manifestation consistent with hypercortisolism resulting from collagen breakdown induced by sustained glucocorticoid excess. The early development of these features in a paediatric patient is consistent with the heightened sensitivity of children to exogenous corticosteroids. Written informed consent for publication of clinical details and images, including identifiable features, was obtained from each patient or their parents/guardian. All patient data were de-identified to protect confidentiality.

findings.label: Unilateral adrenal cortical adenoma
findings.evidence: Caption identifies the patient tumor as a cortisol-producing right adrenal cortical adenoma; the image shows immunohistochemical staining of this tumor.

panels.rationale: Patient-derived adrenal tumor immunohistochemistry supports a functioning adrenal cortical adenoma causing Cushing syndrome. The caption specifically reports strong cytoplasmic CR positivity and focal Syn and CgA positivity. [raw subtype: cortisol-producing adrenal cortical adenoma]

panels.figure_caption: Immunohistochemical staining of the right ACA. Description: Tumor sections were subjected to immunohistochemistry using antibodies against calreticulin (CR), synaptophysin (Syn), and chromogranin A (CgA). The tumor showed strong cytoplasmic positivity for CR, supporting the diagnosis of a cortisol-producing adrenal adenoma. Focal positivity for Syn and CgA was also observed, reflecting partial neuroendocrine differentiation.
